LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. home.blurb: According to an update from the Texans during Thursday night's game, wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip) and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (stinger) would be deemed questionable for a return in the fourth quarter. We ultimately wound up seeing neither return to the action. But given that the Texans were so close to ending the game, it's unclear as to whether or not either player was dealing with a serious injury issue, or were simply being held out for precautionary reasons as the result of the game had already been decided. Rutledge was cleared to return on a short week against the Colts, but now after the same injury has surfaced once again, there might be a slim chance that Houston's first-round rookie is set to miss a little more time moving forward. As for Boutte, his hip injury seems to be a new issue to surface throughout Thursday night, which turned out to be a pretty successful night on his behalf. The Houston Texans put together a commanding win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night en route to a 26-3 victory that might just be the spark needed to help this team rattle off a few wins in a row through the second half of their season. However, in the midst of the Texans winning effort over the Colts, the team also saw their offense suffer a pair of injuries that will be worth keeping an eye on as they approach their next matchup. However, seeing both Boutte and Rutledge go down with an injury––each of whom has their respective key roles on the Texans' offense––is less than an ideal end to an overall successful night for Houston altogether. Kayshon Boutte, Keylan Rutledge Have Injuries to Keep Watch Of One of these injuries has been an issue the Texans have already seen surface earlier in the month, and that's the stinger that Rutledge suffered that makes for his second stinger in the past two weeks. The first stinger for Rutledge was bad enough that it led to him being sidelined for an entire week of the Texans' team practice , along with missing Week 10's game against the Cleveland Browns, forcing fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu into his first-ever start. Boutte converted on both of his targets against the Colts for two catches, 40 yards, and an aggressive touchdown reception in the second quarter for C.J. (Injury Update, Betting Impact for Texans vs. Browns in NFL Week 10) Skip to main content BUY THE ISSUE The Cleveland Browns will get their starting quarterback back in action in Week 10 against the Houston Texans, as Deshaun Watson is off the injury report and set to start. Watson (concussion) missed the team's Week 9 loss to the New Orleans Saints, though backup Shedeur Sanders played pretty decently in his place. Sanders helped get the Browns to overtime, where they lost on a two-point attempt. The second-year quarterback finished the day with 297 passing yards and two scores, carrying the ball for 28 yards on 10 attempts as well. Still, Todd Monken named Watson the starter for Week 10, as the veteran has led the team to a 5-3 record in eight starts with five fourth quarter comeback wins. In the 2026 season, Watson has completed 65.5 percent of his passes for 1,806 yards, seven scores and three interceptions. He's also carried the ball 51 times for 217 yards and a score. He's playing a revenge game against his former team -- Houston -- in Week 10. Even with Watson back, oddsmakers aren't buying the 5-4 Browns in this matchup. They are 4.5-point underdogs at home in the latest odds at DraftKings , even though they have a better record than an underachieving Houston team so far in 2026. Watson is looking to have a big game to keep the starting job, as it's possible the Browns could turn back to Sanders if things go south. Cleveland is still in the playoff picture in the AFC, but it has taken a step back with two straight losses to Pittsburgh and New Orleans. picks.headline: Bills' Undrafted WR Ready for Action vs. Dolphins After Beating Odds Again
picks.blurb: He spent nearly two full seasons on the Buffalo Bills ' practice squad before even getting a sniff of real NFL action . When he finally played in his first career playoff game mote than 2.5 years after signing an undrafted free agent rookie contract, wide receiver Tyrell Shavers tore his ACL. Remarkably, Shavers remained active for the entire second half of the wildcard road win over the Jacksonville Jaguars after suffering the devastating knee injury prior to halftime. Obviously, surgery and an intense rehabilitation process followed, but Shavers worked back into form in just about 10 months' time. His relatively quick return for a wide receiver is another example of beating long odds. Shavers began his collegiate career at Alabama pre-COVID before transferring to Mississippi State. He eventually landed at San Diego State. "He's got one of the best stories out there," said quarterback Josh Allen. "Just how he bounced around in college, coming here, being a P-squad guy, not really getting opportunities, and finally getting his opportunities, and making the most of them. Getting injured, fighting back, and now he's back out here practicing." When will Tyrell Shavers make season debut? His first official practice was on October 28 as the Bills opened his 21-day activation window. Needing to add him to the 53-man roster this week, or lose him for the remainder of the season, Buffalo created a roster spot for Shavers on Monday when it sent seventh-round rookie offensive guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams to Injured Reserve. Shavers was a full participant at practice this week, seemingly aiming to make his season debut when the Miami Dolphins visit Orchard Park for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff on November 22. "The hope is that he'll be up [on Sunday], but a lot of that has to do with, there's a lot of roster moves with some of the injuries and stuff that kind of play into it," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady on Friday afternoon . Last week, the Bills dressed five wide receivers, including return specialist Greg Dortch and fourth-round rookie Skyler Bell. It's presumed that Shavers will take Bell's game day roster spot. Bell has already been a healthy scratch six times this season. "I think he's had a good week in practice," said Brady. "The intent and the hope is that he'll be up, but we'll see what that kinda looks like." Tyrell Shavers's projected role when active Shavers will likely slide in as the Bills' fourth wide receiver, and his eagerness to run block may earn him more snaps on offense. “A lot of trust between me and him," said Allen. "Big body, he'll go up and get it, he'll go in and block duo [run play]. He does all the dirty work. He plays special teams. He never complains. He's where he's supposed to be at all times. He's a great teammate, so very, very happy for him to get back," said Allen. Buffalo has started the year 8-1, sitting atop the AFC East and the AFC as a whole at this time. The Bills have used a strong offensive attack to lead the way, with quarterback Josh Allen gunning for another MVP award. But Allen is more focused on team success, rather than going after any personal accomplishments this season. Allen's focus is on helping the Bills take home the Super Bowl trophy this year, and this entire team feels different this time around. There is still a lot of work to do for this Bills team, with areas that the group can improve on as the year moves forward. But overall, Buffalo's year couldn't have started much better than it already has. As for the upcoming week, Buffalo will be hosting the Miami Dolphins , giving them another chance to grab a win. Miami has struggled this year, going 1-8 for the year so far. The Dolphins will be starting quarterback Kyle McCord again this week, with normal starter Malik Willis injured. McCord threw for 209 yards last week in a loss to the Indianapolis Colts, and the Bills will attempt to throw him off his game. NFL experts Gary Davenport, Brad Gagnon, Kris Knox, Moe Moton, Brent Sobleski, Wes O'Donnell, and Ian Hanford of Bleacher Report made game predictions for each matchup on the schedule this week. Within this, only four of the seven analysts went with the Bills to take down the Dolphins at home. Davenport, Hanford, Knox, and Sobleski were the four to choose the Bills to win, which is a little surprising entering the game. But the Bills will try to grab another win, moving closer to a division title. Given where the two teams are, only having a little over half take Buffalo is interesting, but likely speaks to where Miami is. While the Dolphins haven't been winning games, the team has been competitive all season. Buffalo also has a massive game upcoming next week against the Kansas City Chiefs, and the team could be lacking focus. Oftentimes, games like this could be traps for teams, and the Bills will need to avoid overlooking the Dolphins. Kickoff for the game between the Bills and the Dolphins is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. PT/1:00 p.m. ET.

Since its inception in 1987 on "The Tracy Ullman Show", the nation's longest-running cartoon series and sitcom has become a cultural force with its satirical look at society and culture today. More importantly, it showed Americans that television cartoons can be relished by adults. So I'm hoping you'll catch my meaning when I use a famous Simpsons quote to personify the Buffalo Bills . The NFL team that famously lost four straight Super Bowls in the 1990s is enjoying a Milhouse moment right now. Milhouse Van Houten is Bart Simpson's lovably awkward and loyal best friend. To co-opt a famous Simpsons quote, "everything's comin' up Milhouse" for the 8-1 Bills, who own the best record in the AFC halfway through the regular season. With the hapless Jets in the rearview mirror and the awful Dolphins coming to town, it's a great time for Bills fans to enjoy the AFC's best record at the season's halfway point. Will it stay that way for the NFL's most cursed franchise? Who knows. The early predictions for the Bills vs. Dolphins matchup this week are decidedly in Buffalo's favor. So, maybe this Milhouse moment is sticking around. Bills vs. Dolphins odds (Odds as of Monday afternoon) The Bills are 16.5-point favorites. The over/under is 45.5 points. The money line for the Bills is -1400 (bet $1,400 to win $100) and the Raiders are +950 (bet $100 to win $950). Now let's look at a sample of the early predictions: Democrat and Chronicle: Bills 38, Dolphins 13 Sal Maiorana writes: "The Dolphins have started a season 1-8 or worse for just the fourth time in franchise history, the last coming when they began 2007 with 13 straight losses on the way to a franchise-worst 1-15 record. On paper, this is the most one-sided matchup of the season in the NFL, and with the game being played at Highmark Stadium, it's highly unlikely that the Bills will stub their toe. "After this game, Buffalo has a tremendously difficult five-game stretch that will probably determine whether they can grab the AFC's No. 1 seed for the first time since 1993. The Bills have won their last three games by a combined 62 points and Brady will have the Bills ready to go for what should easily be another 20-plus point victory." AZCentral.com: Bills 31, Dolphins 14 Jeremy Cluff writes: "The Bills opened as a massive 16.5-point favorite against the Dolphins. Will Buffalo win a sixth straight game? Yes, it will. Josh Allen will deliver as Buffalo hands Miami a fourth straight loss." Bookies.Com: Take the under Bill Speros writes: "The Bills (8-1 SU and 7-2 ATS) tore up the Jets 31-12 in Week 10 and are off to the franchise's best start in 35 years. The Bills' combo of Josh Allen and James Cook bludgeons opposing defenses. The 1-8 Dolphins are a surprising 5-4 ATS, and this is the largest NFL spread of the season so far. away.headline: Dolphins get encouraging injury news on two receivers before Bills game
away.blurb: Miami’s passing game could have more help available Sunday as the Dolphins prepare for their AFC East matchup with the Buffalo Bills . Douglas is dealing with a shoulder injury, while Bell has been working back from a knee injury that kept him out of Miami’s last game against the Indianapolis Colts. According to the Dolphins’ official injury report, both receivers were limited participants in practice Wednesday and Thursday, His expected return would give quarterback Kyle McCord another receiving option after Miami fell 24-22 at Indianapolis on Nov. 15. Washington threw a 34-yard touchdown pass to Tolbert on a trick play against the Colts, providing one of Miami’s biggest offensive moments. He snagged Miami’s longest reception against Indianapolis and helped create a scoring opportunity while the Dolphins were trying to erase a second-half deficit. The encouraging news does not resolve every concern at receiver, however. Jared Wayne missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices with a quadriceps injury, leaving another availability question for Miami to address. The Dolphins visit Buffalo on Sunday, Nov. 22, with kickoff scheduled for 1 p.m. ET. away.headline: Dolphins Final Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Trending Up, Trader Trending Down
away.blurb: Even though the Miami Dolphins listed center Aaron Brewer as questionable for their Week 11 game against the Buffalo Bills, all signs are pointing toward him being able to play Sunday. Brewer took the final step toward getting out of the concussion protocol when he took part in a full practice Friday, and the only hurdle remaining will be reporting no symptoms Saturday. The Dolphins did rule out two players Friday, punter Bradley Pinion and wide receiver Jared Wayne. The Dolphins listed two other players as doubtful, including starting safety Dante Trader Jr., but it's difficult to envision him playing after he didn't practice all week. Also listed as doubtful was cornerback Jaylin Simpson, who's dealing with a knee injury. He's mainly a special teams contributor and Baker might wind up taking his place. The best projection if Trader indeed is out against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Like the Dolphins, the Bills ruled out two players Friday and both happen to be starters on defense, cornerback Christian Benford and linebacker Dorian Williams The Bills also have injury issues at tight end, which could impact to some degree their running game. Starter Dalton Kincaid was listed as doubtful after not practicing all week because of thumb and ankle issues, while Jackson Hawes was listed as questionable after being limited all week. The Bills had two others listed as questionable, safety Damar Hamlin (toe) and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (shoulder). It's a fair expectation then that Brewer will be back in the lineup after missing the game against the Indianapolis Colts. Replacing Wayne will be simple because veteran Jalen Tolbert again will be active. Fellow wide receivers Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell both were full participants in practice Friday and did not get a game status designation, meaning they're good to go. Recent acquisition Jack Browning will do the punting after being signed to the practice squad this week, and it's probably fair to assume he'll simply be elevated for the game. The Dolphins also will look to the practice squad for kicker Daniel Carlson and likely defensive tackle Matthew Butler, but with only two elevations allowed, one will have to be signed to the 53-man roster. The Dolphins also could have to make room for cornerback Darrell Baker Jr., who was a full participant all week and appears ready to contribute on special teams. It will make for another interesting Saturday of personnel moves. The only other Dolphins player with a game status designation was cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr., who has been a healthy scratch in recent weeks. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

away.headline: Dolphins Injury Report Week 11: 5 Players Miss Practice

Miami also made a move to sign a punter to the practice squad, bringing in Jack Browning. That is not a guarantee that Pinion will be out, but it is an insurance move for sure. The rest of the DNP players might be upgraded on the additional injury reports. Long snapper Tucker (shoulder), wide receiver Chris Bell (knee), cornerback Juju Brents (neck), wide receiver Caleb Douglas (shoulder), and center Andrew Meyer (neck) were all limited. Miami will need to have its top players available if they want a chance to hang with the surging Bills. Defensive lineman Zach Sieler was already out for the season with a ruptured biceps, and he has now been joined by both Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
away.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Shough was spotted practicing without the protective glove he had been wearing on his injured hand, according to Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football, who reported the development on Thursday, November 19. "Tyler Shough is no longer wearing a glove on his left hand at practice," Underhill reported. It's a small change with potentially significant implications for the Saints quarterback, who has been playing through two reported broken bones in his non-throwing hand. While the absence of the glove does not necessarily mean Shough is fully healed, it represents an encouraging development ahead of New Orleans' November 22 matchup against the Chicago Bears. Tyler Shough's Broken Hand Has Affected Saints Offense Shough's injury first became a concern in early October, when the quarterback was seen with his left hand heavily wrapped during the Saints' game against the Minnesota Vikings. As Heavy previously reported , head coach Kellen Moore was questioned about the severity of the injury but initially stopped short of confirming whether Shough had suffered a fracture. ESPN's Adam Schefter subsequently reported on October 18 that Shough was playing through two broken bones in his left hand. I did that the past two weeks. After a good Week 9 picking games, I was solid again in Week 10. I went 9-5 against the spread and 8-6 straight up. I'll take it. Two weeks in a row. Wow. The records after 10 weeks are now 95-54-1 straight up and 68-79-3 ATS. Climbing out of a huge hole, ATS has me now visibly seeing the .500 mark. Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Even so, look for the Cowboys offense to have a big day throwing it against a Tennessee defense that struggles against the pass. Dak Prescott will put up big numbers. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. The Chiefs are coming off an impressive road victory in which Patrick Mahomes threw five touchdown passes. The defense is third in the league in scoring. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. Pick: Chiefs 33, Cardinals 14 Pittsburgh Steelers (-4.5) at Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are coming off a bye, while the Steelers are coming off a loss to division-rival Cincinnati. The Eagles are a shell of the team they were early in the season because of injuries and trades. This battle of Pennsylvania has lost some luster. Look for the Steelers to bounce back with a tough defensive effort against an undermanned offense, and Aaron Rodgers will play well. Pick: Steelers 26, Eagles 13 Baltimore Ravens (+2.5) at Carolina Panthers Both of these teams are in desperation mode when it comes to needing victories for the postseason. The Ravens lost at home Monday night to the previously winless Chargers and now have to head out on the road on a short week. That's tough. The Panthers played better defense last week against the Saints, which will help them here. Carolina wins it late, but it's close. Pick: Panthers 23, Ravens 22 New York Jets at Los Angeles Chargers (-3.5) Sunday, 4:05 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Chargers won for the first time on Monday night, beating the Ravens on the road. They actually showed some offensive life in that game. The Jets have defensive issues, which the Chargers can take advantage of here. Quarterback Geno Smith is banged up for the Jets, which could mean rookie Cade Klubnik makes his first NFL start. Look for the Chargers to take advantage if that is the case as they get to 2-8 behind another solid showing by the offense. Pick: Chargers 28, Jets 24 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Sunday, 4:25 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Fernando Mendoza will be making his first road start, which can be tough for a rookie. But it's also against a really good defense coming off a bye in a tough place to play. That's a real challenge. Look for the Broncos to get after him in this one. The Raiders ' defense isn't playing well, so maybe it's just what Bo Nix needs. Broncos big. Pick: Broncos 31, Raiders 14 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants This is a big game for both teams. The Jaguars are 7-2 and playing as well as any team in the league. But they are playing consecutive road games against a Giants team pushing for a division title. This game will be decided by the Giants' defense against the Jaguars' offense. I think the Jaguars get the better of it. Look for them to run it well with Bhayshul Tuten . Pick: Jaguars 26, Giants 17 Minnesota Vikings at San Francisco 49ers (-3) In Mexico, Sunday, 8:20 p.m. on NBC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) This is the best game of the week, featuring two of the NFC's best. The 49ers beat Dallas last week, while the Vikings beat the Packers in Kirk Cousins ' first game back with the team after being traded by the Raiders. This will be about the 49ers offense vs. Brian Flores' defense. I think Kyle Shanahan will get the best of it as the 49ers keep rolling. Big day for Christian McCaffrey running it. Pick: 49ers 23, Vikings 16 Cincinnati Bengals at Washington Commanders (+6.5) Monday, 8:15 p.m. on ESPN, ABC (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bengals are rolling on offense as Joe Burrow pushes toward the MVP. The Commanders have had problems against the pass, ranking 31st in the league, which has to have Burrow and the offense ready to go. Jayden Daniels won't keep up, but it's close. The Bengals keep rolling. Pick: Bengals 34, Commanders 30 Indianapolis Colts (+12.5) at Houston Texans Thursday, 8:15 p.m. on Amazon Prime If the Texans are to have any chance of making the playoffs, they have to win this one. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. The Titans' previous two opponents have crossed the 40 mark, and Dallas, in spite of their loss, score as much against a better 49ers defense this past week. Dallas is a veteran-led group in the middle of a difficult year; their down season can't be compared to that of the Titans, and QB Dak Prescott is sure to run this defense through the ringer. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. A lot has to go right, but this game wouldn't have been seen as winnable only a few short weeks ago. For that reason, I believe the Titans will win it. picks.headline: Staff Predictions for Titans vs. Cowboys: A Close Game Across the Board, But Split 2 Ways on the Result
picks.blurb: Last week, the Titans On SI staff predicted an unfortunate defeat at the hands of the Jacksonville Jaguars. That came to pass, but not without enough positive momentum for a few of us to change our tune this week. The Titans enter Dallas with just one win in nine tries, and as of now, the top pick in the 2027 draft. Every discussion around this team is double-edged; the future takes hold on the now for a team in the Titans' position. For Sunday's Week 11 matchup with the Cowboys, the staff are evenly divided. Here are our individual cases for the outcome: Isaiah: Titans 34, Cowboys 38 In recent weeks, the Tennessee Titans have produced positive trends that have me cautiously optimistic heading into Jerry’s World, especially with QB Cam Ward seeming to find his stride. However, the Titans’ defense has fallen apart. Across their last three matchups, Tennessee has allowed an average of 36 points per game, including back-to-back games of at least 40 points given up.Although the Cowboys’ defense hasn’t lived up to expectations, QB Dak Prescott has led Dallas to a top-five scoring offense with an average of nearly 29 points per game. Dallas has the offensive weapons to dominate an underwhelming Tennessee secondary. I anticipate even a herculean effort from ex-Cowboys RB Tony Pollard can’t undo the Titans’ defensive errors from another loss. Lane: Titans 30, Cowboys 27 The Titans are 1-8 coming off a 17-point loss, but I feel good about the team's chances this week. It helps that Dallas has one of the worst defenses in the league and just swapped their defensive play-callers right before this matchup. It also helps that Cam Ward is on a tear and will return his best pass-catcher on the road this week. Like the rest of the staff, I think it'll come down to the wire. Ultimately, if Tennessee is going to pull away, it will be because Robert Saleh's defense finally finds a way to reward the offense for improving on a weekly basis. Give me the Titans in their second victory of the season in Week 11. Shaun: Titans 33, Cowboys 37 This just feels like the type of game where the Cowboys end up laying an egg and all of the national sports shows spend the week making fun of them because of it.I expect the Titans’ talented young tandem of QB Cam Ward and WR Carnell Tate to make their presence felt throughout the contest as they play together for the first time in nearly a month. It also wouldn’t shock me if RB Tony Pollard ends up having a big day against his former team.But with the Titans’ defensive struggles being just as bad, if not worse than Dallas’, I think the Titans end up falling just short in a game that produces a lot of points by both teams. Dharya: Titans 27, Cowboys 24 Tennessee’s offense is finally gaining momentum, while Dallas’s defense is going in the opposite direction. If Brian Daboll’s unit can play efficient, mistake-free football, and Robert Saleh’s defense holds Dak Prescott and the dynamic Cowboys’ offense in check, the Titans should pick up their second win of the year. The Titans have all the ingredients for an upset here. We'll see if the team can finally put together a complete game and pull off the win. (Chitose Suzuki/The Dallas Morning News) SportsDay Staff · Dallas Morning News Fri, November 20, 2026 at 4:23 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's been a week of change for the Dallas Cowboys . Will it lead to results on the field? After a tough defeat at the hands of the San Francisco 49ers, and a change at defensive play-caller , the Tennessee Titans head to AT&T Stadium to deliver the next test to the Cowboys' defense. Can they rebound under Mike Pettine? The Dallas Morning News ' columnists and beat writers gave their predictions below. Tim Cowlishaw The Titans may be headed for another top pick in the draft, but their offense is keeping them in games, averaging 27.2 points per game the last four. Expect explosive plays from Tony Pollard. Where are the Cowboys mentally after seeing yet another change on defense with Mike Pettine now sending in plays instead of Christian Parker? Cowboys' injury list was their friend the first half of the season but significant players are now missing time. Not the cakewalk the point spread suggests for Dallas. Titans 30, Cowboys 22 Change can cause a spark, no doubt. It's why it wouldn't be a surprise to see the Cowboys' defense have an immediate improvement with Mike Pettine calling plays, rather than defensive coordinator Christian Parker. I'm just not ready to believe yet. Just as the Cowboys lost to the lowly Cardinals and Buccaneers (at the time), I think there's a real chance they could lose to the one-win Titans, as well. Titans 31, Cowboys 27 The Cowboys changed defensive play-callers but the defensive players remain. They will continue to give up big plays and big points to a Titans offense that is better than some realize. But this game, and the Thanksgiving matchup against the Eagles, will determine the fate of the Cowboys' season. If there is any hope of digging out of the hole they've created, they must win these next two. That extra motivation will be just enough to carry the home team. Cowboys 30, Titans 28 Abraham Nudelstejer On paper, the Titans are a beatable opponent. Then again, the Buccaneers looked beatable. So did the Cardinals. For Cam Ward, this game presents a golden opportunity to remind everyone why he was the No. 1 overall pick in last year's draft. Facing a Dallas defense that has struggled throughout the season and already cost its coordinator his play-calling duties, Ward has a chance to deliver the best performance of his young career. As for the Cowboys, there is little evidence that a turnaround is imminent. Dallas is just 1-3 at home, has scored 123 points and allowed exactly the same number, all while its owner watches in astonishment. Titans 27, Cowboys 24 Kevin Sherrington Now that Christian Parker's no longer a target, attention turns back the head coach. Beating Tennessee offers only a temporary respite for a beleaguered staff. They're all just dead men walking. The only way they can save themselves is winning the division, then winning at least one playoff game. Nothing less will do, and even that's not enough. Cowboys 31, Titans 20 Calvin Watkins The Cowboys went through a tough week talking about the changes with Christian Parker's role. Now comes the game, and while the Titans' record shows they are terrible, there is some talent on the roster. Dallas has more talent and should have one of its easiest wins of the year. away.headline: Tennessee Titans injury report: Carnell Tate, Anthony Hill Jr. limited
Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10
away.blurb: But what about Tate and four other major players missing the contest? That isn't even mentioning another questionable designation on, you guessed it, the offensive side of the ball. Robert Saleh's post-bye goal was for this team to come out swinging. On top of that laundry list, RB Tyjae Spears is once again questionable. Spears hasn't played since October 18, in the Titans' win over the Indianapolis Colts. Forgive our staff for entering tomorrow with a pessimistic mindset , but things simply aren't falling in a positive way for Tennessee. Of course, this doesn't negate the positive draft capital the team acquired at the deadline, nor does it cancel out Ward's progress. LB Cedric Gray missed Week 1 due to a concussion, and has still yet to return to the leading role he held last season. The Titans aren't 1-7 because of injuries, but setbacks like these have arguably led to the team ending up on the wrong side of the five one-score games they've lost. Titans' Overloaded Injury Report May Put an Upset Over Jaguars on Ice in Week 10 Skip to main content SI.COM Carnell Tate missing the Tennessee Titans' Week 8 matchup wasn't enough to derail the offense from their best performance of the season. Even in a loss, Tennessee posted 36 points and ground up some real momentum for the first time in weeks heading into the bye. That in itself isn't the issue, but it's hard to really land a hit when you're missing a hand. The Titans, in addition to Tate, will be without LBs Anthony Hill Jr. and Cody Barton, G Peter Skoronski, and P Tommy Townsend. The latter two were sent to the injured reserve list today. Titans are losing major players at the worst possible time This is a team coming apart at the seams at the worst time. One-instance absences - like Tate's in Week 8 - are easier to handle. But the Titans are a 1-7 squad down five starters against the best team in their division. However, it does mean that a Tennessee team down on their luck have caught another bad break. Tennessee can't catch a break this season You'll recall an 0-2 Titans team in a winnable situation on the road watching rookie RG Fernando Carmona Jr. exit vs. the New York Giants. Tennessee lost that game 12-7, and are just now trying to get Carmona back into the swing of things in practice. From that point of view, Week 10's injury report isn't all that surprising. Although, as the season winds down and certain decisions have to be made about this roster prior to an especially important draft, the added pressure from being down impactful talent works against the Titans' rebuilding process. We'll see how the undermanned team fares tomorrow, but for those hoping for a turnaround-sparking upset, you may want to splash cold water on that optimism ahead of time. home.headline: Horrific injuries revealed in Cowboys fan death as family says 49ers supporter blamed by victim
home.blurb: “Let me make the point of, we really do have quite a — eons above what it was 10, 15 years ago — we have quite a surveillance of what’s going on at every aspect of our game. And so it is really rare if we didn’t know of any incident. We’ve got too many people out there; we have 6,000 workers on game day,” Jones continued. A 36-year-old Dallas Cowboys fan died after an alleged altercation at AT&T Stadium claimed a 49ers fan pushed him down a flight of stairs, causing a “bulge of blood” in his stomach, according to his heartbroken family. Mario Narro traveled from Albuquerque, New Mexico, to Arlington, Texas, last weekend to watch his beloved Cowboys face the San Francisco 49ers in one of the NFL’s most storied rivalries on Sunday, Nov. 15, his niece Claudia DeLara told the California Post. Narro told a friend he attended the game with that he had gotten into a scuffle and was pushed down a flight of stairs by a Niners fan, DeLara said. “He got pushed,” DeLara claimed. “He fell. And immediately he had bruising and swelling in his abdomen.” Narro continued to watch the game after the fall, DeLara said, but after the final whistle on the Niners’ 46-40 victory over the Cowboys, “his friends knew that he was off.” “He wasn’t feeling like his normal self and acting like his normal self and so they made him show them his abdomen just to check to see,” DeLara told The Post. “And they said they could visibly see the bruising and, like, a bulge of blood in his abdomen,” she added. Narro’s friends rushed him to stadium medics, who transported him to a nearby hospital. He continued to insist a Niners fan had pushed him, repeating the account to doctors, DeLara said. Narro then underwent several emergency surgeries, but died from his injuries Wednesday morning. The family is still in the dark as to a specific cause of death, DeLara said. The Tarrant County Medical Examiner is conducting further testing to determine the official cause and manner of Narro’s death. “Nobody really knows what happened,” DeLara added. “We did file a police report because the only thing that we have is [Narro] said that a 49ers fan pushed him. He said that to his friend and the medical team. We don’t know what happened otherwise.” The Arlington Police Department was notified of Narro’s death on Wednesday and is currently “treating this case as a death investigation,” according to a department spokesperson. “The investigation is ongoing,” the APD added. Narro, a lifelong Cowboys fan who loved to travel and crack jokes, had visited AT&T Stadium at least two or three times before Sunday, DeLara said. “He just loved the team,” she said. Narro’s niece, Catalina Jenkins, added that she believes her uncle would still be alive “if it weren’t for this football game.” “I just want it to be clear he was an angel of a man, never hurt anyone, never had anything bad to say about anyone,” Jenkins said. “He was so loved. picks.blurb: Odds Detroit Lions Beat Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 11 Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI On Sunday, the Detroit Lions could be facing a Tampa Bay Buccaneers team devoid of two of its top players: QB Baker Mayfield (foot injury) and S Antoine Winfield Jr. (ankle). Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers. Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three). Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. Tez Johnson catches a 40-yard pass Nov 8, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers wide receiver Tez Johnson (15) makes a catch past Chicago Bears cornerback Kyler Gordon (6) in the second half at Soldier Field. Mandatory Credit: Talia Sprague-Imagn Images Johnson has only 11 catches, but he's averaging 23.1 yards per reception with a long of 64, according to ESPN . Nobody else on the roster with more than five catches is close to that average. Detroit is playing without Aidan Hutchinson, and the Lions will have to respect Irving and the run game. One play-action shot to Johnson is the easiest way for a quarterback on a sore foot to change the game without having to move much. 3. The Bucs intercept Jared Goff twice Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers cornerback Jacob Parrish (25) intercepts a pass intended for Atlanta Falcons wide receiver Drake London (5) thrown by quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (not pictured) during the second quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Goff has thrown four interceptions all season, so this one is bold. Tampa Bay has 21 takeaways , and 16 of them are interceptions. Zyon McCollum and Alex Anzalone have four apiece, and Jacob Parrish has two. Parrish draws Amon-Ra St. Brown, and he's PFF's No. 4 cornerback . If Goff keeps feeding St. Brown against Bowles' zone looks, the Bucs will get a couple of chances to jump a route. 4. Tampa Bay wins its first one-score game Nov 1, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Buccaneers placekicker Chase McLaughlin (4) celebrates with punter Riley Dixon (9) after kicking a thirty-four-yard field goal against the Atlanta Falcons during the first quarter at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images The Bucs' three wins came by eight, 30 and 16 points. Every loss has been by seven or fewer, and the red zone is a big reason. Tampa Bay has scored touchdowns on 15 of its 31 trips inside the 20 and settled for field goals on 12 others. That's why this ends with Chase McLaughlin. He's made all 22 of his field-goal attempts this season, and a close game in Detroit finally breaks Tampa Bay's way on his leg. Bucs 23, Lions 21. picks.blurb: Before the Roar: Previewing Lions vs. Buccaneers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Before the Roar: Previewing Lions vs. Buccaneers Morgan Cannon · SB Nation Fri, November 20, 2026 at 6:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads With their trip across the pond now in the rearview mirror, the Detroit Lions are fresh off of their 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany and looking to keep their winning ways rolling in Week 11 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Despite their 3-6 record, Tampa Bay is firmly in the NFC South hunt, and their stingy defense is one of the biggest reasons why. To break down the defense and everything else ahead of the game, Meko Scott and I are back with another episode of, " Before the Roar ." We start out with a Buccaneers' quarterback situation that seems like it's a fluid one as the week progresses. Initially, it seemed like quarterback Baker Mayfield was a bit of a longshot to play against the Lions, especially considering the moves Tampa Bay made when they signed free agent quarterback Cooper Rush, and elevated Easton Stick to the active roster from the practice squad. However, in a recent interview, Mayfield made it seem as though he would be playing if he can get cleared by Tampa Bay's medical staff. Ultimately, whoever ends up at quarterback really won't change the Lions' gameplan all that much. It all is going to hinge on Detroit's ability to stop the Buccaneers' running game. On the opposite side of the ball, the Buccaneers' defense is arguably the best in the NFL. From front-seven players like rookie linebacker Josiah Trotter and veteran nose tackle Vita Vea, to a secondary that includes the likes of Zyon McCollum and Antoine Winfield Jr, it's easy to see why this defense is so effective against just about anything that opposing offenses throw at them. Walker's increased playing time is particularly important with Yaya Diaby dealing with a knee injury, although the available reporting does not establish that Walker's entire increase resulted from Diaby's absence. Injuries forced Tampa Bay to adjust before the bye, but the increased playing time also created opportunities to evaluate its depth. Chukwuma and Johnson showed they could contribute when starters were unavailable, while Durham, Sharp, and Walker earned bigger roles that could remain valuable in the second half of the season. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers entered their Week 10 bye having dealt with injuries at quarterback, wide receiver, offensive tackle, and across the defense. Those absences forced lineup adjustments, but they also gave other players chances to show what they could contribute when called upon to step up. According to DepthRoom's snap-count data , five Buccaneers increased their share of playing time by at least 10 percentage points when comparing Weeks 4–6 with Weeks 7–9. Some stepped in for injured starters, while others saw their roles expand as personnel usage changed. Chukwuma saw the biggest increase, rising from 0% of Tampa Bay's offensive snaps in Weeks 4–6 to 33% over the next three games. His opportunity came when Luke Goedeke missed Week 7 against Carolina with a calf injury. Chukwuma started at right tackle and helped Tampa Bay rush for 258 yards in a 43-13 victory. According to Scott Smith's official team report , it was Chukwuma's third career start, and Todd Bowles expressed confidence in his potential to become a full-time NFL starter. Johnson's snap share climbed from 43% to 62%, with Emeka Egbuka's absence opening a spot at wide receiver. Egbuka missed Weeks 7 and 8 while dealing with concussion and foot injuries. Johnson started against Carolina and played 41 offensive snaps, contributing a 19-yard third-down reception, a 14-yard rushing gain, and a 14-yard touchdown catch. His involvement continued growing after Egbuka returned, reaching 54 snaps, or 79% of the offense, against Chicago in Week 9. away.headline: Buccaneers May Need Rookie QB Jalon Daniels at the Worst Time
away.blurb: Mayfield’s availability remains the central variable. If he can return, the Buccaneers gain their veteran starter for an important NFC road test. If he cannot, Daniels’ legs, decision-making, and ability to avoid costly possessions will determine whether Tampa Bay can make its rushing attack the centerpiece of a credible upset bid. – The Lions placed linebacker Jack Campbell (neck) on injured reserve, while edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson (knee) is out for the season. Those absences could make Daniels’ scrambling ability and Tampa Bay’s ground game more consequential if the rookie starts. Buccaneers’ Keionte Scott Earns Rookie Recognition, but One Flaw Stands Out Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield (leg) has an uncertain outlook for Sunday’s (Nov. 22) road game against the Detroit Lions, creating the possibility rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make another start. The Buccaneers need Mayfield’s status clarified quickly because Daniels’ mobility could change the offense’s approach in a matchup expected to hinge on controlling possession, protecting the football, and keeping Detroit’s high-powered attack off the field. Locked On Bucs host James Yarcho said Daniels took the first-team reps after Mayfield missed Wednesday’s practice. The official team preview also listed Mayfield’s lower-leg injury as a major question for the week and noted Tampa Bay promoted Easton Stick from the practice squad, underscoring the need for quarterback insurance. Daniels has started three games while Mayfield was sidelined. He has supplied a dimension the offense can use if he starts again. He has rushed 22 times for 123 yards, a 5.6-yard average, while completing 60 of 98 passes for 501 yards, three touchdowns, and five interceptions. Yarcho does not suggest Daniels is the more polished passer, but rather his ability to escape the pocket could extend drives against a Lions defense missing key front-seven pieces. That mobility matters most if it helps running back Bucky Irving sustain Tampa Bay’s preferred game script. Irving has 825 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through nine games, and the Buccaneers have leaned on him heavily during their recent stretch. A Daniels start would put more pressure on the offense to pair designed quarterback movement, play-action and a disciplined rushing attack rather than asking the rookie to win a pass-heavy game from the pocket. – Irving remains the offensive centerpiece, but the Buccaneers have also discussed reducing his workload after he logged 111 carries over the previous five games. Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker could take on more work if Tampa Bay wants to preserve Irving while maintaining its physical identity. – Detroit running back Jahmyr Gibbs presents the defining test for the defense after reaching 1,000 rushing yards in nine games. Yarcho argued that limiting Gibbs on the ground and as a receiver would give the Buccaneers a better chance to pressure Jared Goff without relying heavily on blitze

home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

picks.headline: 3 Bold Predictions for Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11
picks.blurb: The Arizona Cardinals are 3-7 and headed to Arrowhead Stadium to face a 7-2 Kansas City Chiefs team that just beat Atlanta 35-13. They’ll do it with a 40-year-old quarterback, after Mike LaFleur said rookie Carson Beck’s back spasms have the team preparing Josh Johnson to start . Nobody expects much from Arizona in this one. Here are three bold predictions for Sunday’s noon CT kickoff. 1. Michael Wilson tops 100 receiving yards Kansas City’s defensive plan starts with Trey McBride, who has 78 catches and draws most of the short throws in this offense . That leaves Wilson as the receiver most likely to see single coverage. He has 51 catches for 546 yards, according to ESPN , second on the team behind McBride. We ran his numbers, and they show a receiver who gets volume without many big plays. Wilson has caught 51 of his 89 targets, about 57%, and he’s averaging 60.7 yards per game with a long of 27. A 100-yard day needs one or two downfield completions, and a veteran quarterback who’s been around 15 NFL rosters knows where his second option is. 2. Josh Johnson throws two touchdown passes Johnson is 2-9 in 11 career starts , and Sunday would be his first start since last season with Washington. Arizona has only 13 passing touchdowns in 10 games, and it has scored touchdowns on 42.9% of its red-zone trips. That’s why two touchdown passes is a bold call. Johnson played three games for LaFleur’s Jets in 2021, so he knows the system, and he has McBride as an easy red-zone target. If the Cardinals keep the game close into the second half, Johnson finds him twice. 3. Arizona holds Kansas City under 100 rushing yards This one goes against everything from last week. The Rams ran 46 times for 202 yards against Arizona, and the Cardinals lost two defenders to injured reserve before this trip. Arizona allows 129.9 rushing yards per game, 28th in the league. Kenneth Walker III changes the math, though. He has 872 of Kansas City’s 1,224 rushing yards, about 71%, and he missed practice again Thursday with a groin injury, according to Heavy . If Walker sits for a second straight week, the Chiefs will lean on Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce. Arizona keeps the run game in check and makes Kansas City win it through the air.
