picks.headline: Chiefs-Cardinals betting line & prediction: Kansas City’s biggest mismatch yet?
picks.blurb: Read our AI Policy. Kansas City enters 7-2, while Arizona has lost two straight to fall to 3-7. The betting line lists the Chiefs as 15.5-point favorites over the Cardinals. The prediction picks Kansas City to beat Arizona 33-9 and cover the spread. The Kansas City Chiefs won their second game in a row Sunday when they overpowered the Atlanta Falcons 35-13 , improving to 7-2 on the NFL season. The Arizona Cardinals lost their second straight 34-6 to the Los Angeles Rams to drop to 3-7. Here’s what to know about their matchup on Sunday ... How to watch Cardinals at Chiefs Kickoff: Noon Central Where: Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City TV: CBS (Channel 5 in Kansas City) Radio: KFNZ (96.5 FM in Kansas City, KNSS 98.7 FM in Wichita) Betting line: Chiefs -15.5 Behind the ARI-KC matchup While the Chiefs were getting back on track by taking care of business against the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons over the past two weeks, the Cardinals have been falling apart at the seams. Sunday’s monumental mismatch starts at the quarterback position, where rookie Carson Beck is expected to make his second career start after completing just 11 of 18 passes for 108 yards and two interceptions against the Rams. Arizona has turned to Beck after trading Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and watching last year’s Chiefs backup Gardner Minshew tear the UCL in his throwing arm. Understanding the reality of the situation, linebacker Drue Tranquill showed the two-time national champion with Georgia some respect before outlining the problems he may face against a Chiefs defense that has come alive with eight sacks over the last two games. “He’s obviously got winning pedigree — he did it in college,” Tranquill said of Beck. “He’ll get another start under his belt this week in a great environment, so it’s a good opportunity for him, but we’ll have to execute our pre-snap looks, have to execute our game plan in terms of owning our leverage, taking away options he might want to go to early in the down. And then hopefully, as the game progresses, we can get the pass rush going, get them in known passing situations and get them on the ground.” With running back Jeremiyah Love, the No. 3 overall pick, on injured reserve, the Cardinals’ best path to an upset is extending possessions with veteran back Tyler Allgeier and utilizing first-team All-Pro tight end Trey McBride. McBride has managed 78 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns despite Arizona’s struggles. With wide receivers Kendrick Bourne (tibia) and Michael Wilson (neck) out for the remainder of the season, that’s left McBride as Beck’s lone viable option. Among Arizona’s available players, tight end Elijah Higgins ranks second on the team in receiving yards with 18 catches for 162 yards. “They’ve got some good tight ends, and so we’ll have to be on it,” Tranquill said. “They’re big, they’re physical, can make contested catches. And so we’ll have to own our leverage and be physical at the top of the stem and not allow them to create separation, and try to get the ball off these guys.” Arizona’s protection has allowed 28 sacks this season — tied for the sixth-most in the league. Meanwhile, Chiefs defensive lineman George Karlaftis enters Sunday with at least one sack in each of his last three games , Ashton Gillotte is in the midst of a two-game sack streak and Chris Jones has registered 2.5 sacks over the last two games. The Cardinals’ offensive line is a point to watch, as they played against the Rams without starting center Hjalte Froholdt (concussion) and left tackle Jayden Williams (knee), who had already replaced left tackle Paris Johnson Jr. (biceps tear). Both Froholdt and Williams were limited in practice Wednesday. The situation doesn’t get any easier for the Cardinals on the other side of the ball. In the run game, the Cardinals allow 4.2 yards per carry, and through the air, they give up 8.2 yards per pass attempt. The Chiefs opted to rest Kenneth Walker last Sunday against the Falcons because of groin tightness, and he didn’t practice Wednesday . That means rookie Emmett Johnson could make his second straight start after compiling 171 scrimmage yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off his best passing stat line of the season, in which he threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns against the Falcons. But bigger than that were the chunk gains, as the outing included seven completions of 20 yards or more. While the Cardinals’ secondary is susceptible to explosive passing plays, if there is one area of concern for the Chiefs, it’s that they’re more than capable of generating pressure. Led by safety Budda Baker with 3.5 sacks and outside linebackers Zaven Collins and Josh Sweat with three apiece, the Cardinals have registered 21 sacks this season. “They do a great job of causing havoc and causing pressure, and they do a great job throughout a lot of these football games of kind of stopping the offenses,” Mahomes said. “There’s been parts where offenses have kind of found the big plays, and it has to come within rhythm. It’s not like you can kind of hunt those things. You have to get the ball out of your hand, because if you don’t, they’ll get home, and they’ll cause negative plays.” Protection will be imperative for what could be a shorthanded Chiefs offensive line. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) both missed practice Wednesday, and it remains to be seen whether newly signed veteran Fred Johnson can provide a boost after joining Kansas City’s practice squad Tuesday. In his opening game in a Kansas City uniform , wide receiver Josh Downs turned 11 snaps into four catches for 53 yards and a touchdown. We've gotta figure it out.” The Arizona Cardinals are about to join an unwanted club. Excluding the 1987 strike season, only three teams in the Super Bowl era have ever started four quarterbacks in as many games — until now. Making matters worse, this is the second time that the Cardinals have appeared on the list within the past five years. Start the day smarter. Rams Week 10 injury report vs. Cardinals: Puka Nacua is on IR, so who will step up for LA?
away.blurb: Tyler Higbee stands out as the main weapon to build around in Nacua's absence, particularly on intermediate routes and crucial possession downs. His experience with Stafford makes him a logical candidate for additional attention, although that projection should not be mistaken for an announced target distribution. Higbee's own health briefly complicated that outlook. An illness kept him out Thursday before he returned for limited work Friday. He received no game designation, leaving him available for an offense that needs dependable receiving options. The tight end group's other injuries make his role especially important. Terrance Ferguson is out with ankle and hamstring injuries, while Davis Allen is questionable with an oblique issue. Colby Parkinson offers another available option after progressing to full participation Friday despite injured ribs. Tutu Atwell can provide a different dimension outside. His ability to threaten downfield offers a way to discourage Arizona from crowding shorter routes. Stafford connected with him for a 40-yard gain against the Chargers in Week 8, demonstrating the explosive element available beyond the depleted starting group. CJ Daniels Jr., Xavier Smith and newly promoted Brennan Presley round out the available receiver group. The Rams placed Nacua on IR Thursday to create the roster opening for Presley; Nacua must miss at least four games, making this adjustment more than a one-week assignment. Beyond Nacua's absence, Steve Avila is ruled out after missing every practice with a hamstring injury. Losing an offensive lineman adds another complication as the Rams reshape their passing attack, especially if Stafford needs extra time for unfamiliar combinations to develop. Allen's questionable designation follows limited practices Wednesday and Friday around a missed Thursday session. Long snapper Joe Cardona is also questionable after remaining limited throughout the week with an ankle injury. Defensively, Myles Garrett carries a questionable designation for a knee issue and rest. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday before sitting out Friday. His availability matters after a three-sack performance against Washington helped Los Angeles secure its third consecutive victory. Trent McDuffie and Kam Curl are questionable, too. Both returned for limited work Friday after two missed sessions, managing back and toe injuries, respectively. Braden Fiske missed Friday with an ankle injury but received no game designation. Byron Young and Aaron Donald also sat out for rest without designations, distinguishing their absences from confirmed injury-related setbacks. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. picks.headline: Eagles vs. Steelers: 5 bold predictions for the Week 11 matchup
picks.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
picks.blurb: The Philadelphia Eagles are running out of time to find something resembling an offensive identity. There's hope that the defense catches fire before it's too late. Seven consecutive losses have turned what once looked like a promising season into a weekly search for answers. What's fortunate (or unfortunate depending on your paradigm) is that they're still right in the thick of things in the NFC East. They're four games behind the division-leading New York Giants with seven games remaining. As bad as all four teams have played at times, any team can go on a run or a losing streak and change the complexion of this race for superiority. The upcoming matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers offers another opportunity to see whether anything has changed for the better. The bye week gave Joe Milton extra time to get comfortable with his surroundings and the coaching staff time to address some glaring problems. A turnaround remains difficult to envision, but there are reasons to expect a more competitive performance than Philadelphia has delivered recently. Here are a handful of predictions for the coming contest that reflect both that possibility and the larger issues that continue to hold the Eagles back. DeVonta Smith returns and notches 100 yards receiving while Makai Lemon chips in with 50 DeVonta Smith was very blunt this week . He didn't work so hard during the offseason to 'shut it down' with so many games remaining. "I didn’t get up at 4:30 in the morning all summer just to not play." After limited participation at practice on Wednesday , he got his legs under him a day later and was a full participant on Thursday . He says he's 100 percent healthy. Something tells us an offensively starved Eagles attack will get him the ball early and often against the Steelers . He'll lead the Eagles in targets, receptions, and yards gained. Figure 100 of the latter, but that doesn't mean Makai Lemon will be forgotten. He and Milton have worked together for a while, and that level of comfort should guarantee the former looks for his young rookie to pay dividends. Lemon already showed what his role can look like with Milton. He led the Eagles with six catches for 61 yards on nine targets against the Giants . If Smith returns, Philadelphia can use him outside while keeping Lemon involved on quick throws from the slot. That gives both receivers a path to the yardage totals without asking Milton to spend the afternoon waiting on deep routes. Joe Milton plays turnover-free football There is still plenty to like about Joe Milton's physical ability, but his first start was an especially difficult introduction to life in the NFL . He was thrown into the lineup less than a month after joining the team, behind an offensive line that offered little protection. Even a quarterback with Joe Burrow's experience and ability would have faced a difficult assignment under those circumstances. Milton now has a start behind him and a bye week to prepare for Pittsburgh. He said he would spend much of that time in Philadelphia to build familiarity with the offense and his teammates. A spectacular performance might be too much to expect, but protecting the football and avoiding costly mistakes would represent meaningful progress. Milton went without an interception against New York, but he lost a fumble on a strip-sack by Arvell Reese. Against Pittsburgh, protecting the ball starts with having an answer when the first read is covered and the rush closes in. A checkdown or a throwaway can keep a drive alive without giving the Steelers a short field. Aaron Rodgers throws two interceptions Aaron Rodgers has thrown at least one interception in five of Pittsburgh's nine games this season, and he's been bailed out a few times in games where he hasn't. That's an opportunity Vic Fangio and the Eagles defense should be prepared to exploit, particularly if the pass rush can make the veteran quarterback uncomfortable. Rodgers is experienced enough to recognize pressure and punish defensive mistakes, so forcing him into difficult decisions will be important. Still, Philadelphia has shown it can create disruptive moments defensively. The bold prediction here is that Fangio's unit comes away with two interceptions, even if the Eagles fail to turn both takeaways into points. Two interceptions would be a significant jump for a defense that enters Week 11 with three all season. The best chance starts with pressure from four rushers. If Philadelphia can hurry Rodgers and keep seven defenders in coverage, it can leave help over DK Metcalf while keeping a defender available to break on a shorter throw. Eagles score 20 points despite being one-dimensional Philadelphia's offense has struggled to establish a reliable ground game, and there isn't much reason to expect that the problem has disappeared. Sure, everyone is hopeful, but many have also taken the 'We'll believe it when we see it' approach. Here's the good news. The Steelers have allowed 242.2 passing yards per game. If protection holds up, Milton and the passing attack an opportunity to find some rhythm. The prediction is that Philadelphia hangs a number slightly above Pittsburgh's average. Figure approximately 250 yards through the air thanks to Lemon and some returning reinforcements. The Eagles haven't scored 24 points (a season high) since Week 2. They haven't topped 20 for two weeks, but what the heck? These are bold predictions, right? Call it stubborn. Call it insanity, since a quiet day from the running game is also part of this prediction. Philadelphia hasn't offered a consistent, sustainable formula, but a surprisingly successful air raid and fewer three-and-outs could make this game more high-scoring than expected. Philadelphia loses a game that's closer than most would expect We hate to disappoint you. After all of that, you may have had your fingers crossed for an upset, but the facts are the facts. Right now, Pittsburgh is the better team. The Eagles have opportunities to finally put some points on the board, but Philadelphia has lost seven straight for a reason. As always, the home crowd will be supportive enough to try to provide a spark for a team that desperately needs one. Still, a better offensive showing doesn't automatically solve the team's larger problems. The defense can keep the Eagles within striking distance for much of the afternoon, but eventually the offense must make enough plays to win. Sadly, none of us have seen them do that enough to believe they'll get it done in this scenario. Milton provides a few encouraging moments, but Pittsburgh does enough to offer Philadelphia an eighth consecutive loss. A more watchable performance and a winning result are two very different things, and Philadelphia still has a long way to go before those outcomes become interchangeable. Prediction: Steelers 27, Eagles 20 This article originally appeared on Eagles Wire: Eagles vs. Steelers: 5 bold predictions for the Week 11 matchup

Financial Field on Sunday for a game against their instate rival, the Philadelphia Eagles (2-7). Although on the road, this game comes at a critical point in the Steelers’ season. With games the next three weeks against the Broncos, the Texans, and the Jaguars - all teams contending for a playoff spot in the AFC - this one is a near must-win against the Birds. Second in the AFC North and sixth in the AFC overall, Aaron Rodgers and co. are a half-game ahead of the Browns and 1.5 games ahead of the Patriots in the postseason chase. The Eagles have struggled for most of the season. Jalen Hurts led Philly to wins in their first two games, but the Eagles have since lost every game as well as their quarterback (blood clots). This season, the Steelers have leaned on Rodgers, a productive running game and a defense that ranks among the league leaders in sacks and turnover differential. The veteran signal-caller has thrown for 2,014 yards with 15 touchdowns and six interceptions, while Jaylen Warren has rushed for 719 yards. Philadelphia’s season has unraveled in large part because of injuries, most notably the aforementioned loss of Hurts to injured reserve with blood clots. That leaves Joe Milton III directing an Eagles offense averaging just 16.4 points and an NFL-low 260.2 yards per game. Pittsburgh’s four-game winning streak came to an abrupt end last Sunday in a 38-18 road loss to Cincinnati. The Bengals completely suffocated the Steelers with Pittsburgh managing only 23 total yards through the first three quarters before producing some offense and points after the game was out of reach. DK Metcalf was held without a catch through three quarters before finishing with two receptions for 54 yards and a touchdown, while the defense spent far too much time on the field. Philadelphia, meanwhile, comes into Sunday’s game rested after its bye but desperately searching for an answer to a disastrous stretch. The bye, though, may help an injury-ravaged roster: receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) could return after missing the Giants game. The Eagles lead the all-time series 50-29-3, and Pittsburgh has endured an extraordinary drought in Philadelphia. The Steelers have not won in Philly since 1965. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Wide receiver DeVonta Smith was upgraded to a full participant on Thursday after practicing in a limited capacity Wednesday. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. Linebacker Smael Mondon joined fellow linebacker Zack Baun on the sideline Thursday. Mondon was a full participant with an ankle injury on Wednesday, but did not participate in practice Thursday. Mondon stepped in during the Week 9 game against the Giants before the bye week after Baun suffered a back injury and Jihaad Campbell was out with hamstring and quad injuries. Baun has yet to practice this week, while Campbell is on track to return. Running back Will Shipley, practicing for the first time since the Week 5 game in London, was limited for the second straight day. The Eagles would need to activate him off of Injured Reserve to be eligible for Sunday's game. RB Will Shipley and WR Dontayvion Wicks spotted! Let's hope the hot streak stays as we move towards Thanksgiving. There are a ton of big spreads this week, so watch out. The dogs might be barking. All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET Miami Dolphins (+16.5) at Buffalo Bills Sunday, 1 p.m. on CBS (Stream on Paramount+ ) Miami is playing consecutive road games after losing at Indianapolis, while the Bills are home for the first time after two road games. The Bills are playing better on defense in recent weeks against some lower-level quarterbacks. They get another one here in backup Kyle McCord . The Bills will score, as Josh Allen always plays well against Miami, but Miami stays around. Pick: Bills 31, Dolphins 19 New Orleans Saints (+11.5) at Chicago Bears Sunday, 1 p.m. on Fox (Stream: Fubo -- try for free) The Bears are off a bye, while the Saints lost to the Panthers last week. Chicago is much improved on defense. With the Saints unable to run the ball, it will put a lot of pressure on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough . Caleb Williams will bounce back from his four-interception game last time out against Tampa Bay and will play well here. Bears take it. Pick: Bears 24, Saints 16 Tennessee Titans at Dallas Cowboys (-8.5) The Cowboys are bad on defense, but the Titans haven't exactly lit it up on offense. Cam Ward has played better as of late. Pick: Cowboys 37, Titans 23 Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+7) at Detroit Lions The issue here is whether Baker Mayfield will play for the Bucs. If not, they will have big problems. The Lions are back home after beating up the Patriots in Germany last week. The offense was dominant that day, but this Tampa Bay defense is playing well. That will keep them in the game, but the uncertainty at quarterback will be too much to overcome. Pick: Lions 22, Bucs 17 Arizona Cardinals at Kansas City Chiefs (-16.5) Carson Beck makes his first road start for the Cardinals and this is as tough as any place in the league to do so. That will make for a tough day for this limited Arizona offense. Blowout. The Bengals keep rolling. The Colts are pretty much done, but they beat Miami last week. Daniel Jones struggled in that one, but the Texans' defense has really struggled. Look for the Colts to hang around here, but the Texans will win it. away.headline: NFL fans react to Ravens’ rumored plan for Lamar Jackson’s return after thumb injury
away.blurb: The Baltimore Ravens believe Lamar Jackson has a chance to return from his broken right thumb for their Week 16 game against the Cleveland Browns on Dec. 27 if his rehab goes smoothly, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported this week. Lamar Jackson’s Road From Buffalo Toward a Possible Browns Return In a statement the team released that day, head coach Jesse Minter called recovery timelines “challenging to predict” and said, “He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return.” Minter added, “We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season.” Graziano’s report hinges on Jackson’s progress in the same way, leaving the Browns game at M&T Bank Stadium a possibility rather than a set date for his return. For another fan, the calendar is the problem, since a return against the Browns would leave Jackson only two more regular-season games after that one. A Dec. 27 return would be near the optimistic end of Jackson’s reported recovery timetable, though the Ravens have emphasized that his progress, rather than a fixed date, will determine when he can play again. The report comes with Baltimore at 4-6, days after a 23-20 home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers, who had not won a game before Monday night. Despite the prospect of Jackson returning for the final stretch of the regular season, several fans who responded to the report argued that the Ravens should keep him sidelined and focus on having him healthy for 2027. Jackson’s injury came on Baltimore’s first offensive play of the Nov. 1 game at Buffalo, a 36-10 loss, when his throwing hand caught the arm of Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau as he threw. On Nov. 13, the Ravens said the thumb was dislocated and broken and that the injury typically carries a recovery of six to 10 weeks. Sources told ESPN’s Adam Schefter that Jackson had undergone surgery the week before. Fans Point to the Baltimore Ravens’ Slide and Jackson’s Long-Term Health “Week 16 is so late. Just shut him down and run it back next year,” the fan wrote. Baltimore’s form has added to the argument. The Ravens sit fourth in the AFC North and have lost five straight games, including the Buffalo game in which Jackson was hurt and both games since. Jacoby Brissett, whom Baltimore acquired in a trade, started in Jackson’s place in the loss to the Chargers. “It’s already over … just take the rest of the season off,” another fan responded. Jackson’s health is another piece of it. A high ankle sprain had already cost him three games before the thumb injury, and he has played just 14 full quarters this season. A fan pointed to that history: “Yea bro let’s have Lamar play meaningless games in a lost season after 2 major injuries.” Others looked straight ahead to next season. “What’s the point to play him at that point, come back ’27 stronger,” one fan wrote. away.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. home.blurb: Ravens Final Injury Report Week 11: Nnamdi Madubuike Out vs Panthers - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Ravens Final Injury Report Week 11: Nnamdi Madubuike Out vs Panthers Ahead of the matchup, the final injury report has been released. Multiple players are out, including defensive lineman Nnmamdi Madubuike. As stated above, Madubuike has been ruled out due to the hamstring injury that he suffered on Monday against the Los Angeles Chargers. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins is also out as he is dealing with a nagging knee injury. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey is also out, as head coach Jesse Minter made the decision to send the defender home after he made disparaging comments about the city of Baltimore on his podcast. This includes rookie guard Vega Ioane, who was upgraded from a limited participant with shoulder and knee injuries. Ioane was also ruled out of the Chargers matchup after suffering the shoulder injury. Despite being limited to start the week, the rookie is ready to go. Rookie running back Adam Randall is also set to play after his return. Randall suffered neck and hamstring injuries during training camp and has yet to play a game in the regular season. The Ravens have a tall task ahead, as they are searching to snap their five-game losing streak. Currently, the team sits at 4-6 and is a couple more losses away from losing out on the postseason. There is no guarantee that ending the season 9-8 or 10-7 will or won't keep Baltimore out of the playoffs, but history has shown teams that end with a 10-7 record have an increasingly more difficult time making it into the postseason. Winning out will be crucial and the best course of action for the Ravens to make the playoffs. It starts with the Panthers on Sunday. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 4:54 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It's tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It's come to this: the Jets aren't even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! picks.headline: Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11
picks.blurb: Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Chargers Unanimously Picked By ESPN Experts to Defeat Jets in Week 11 (James Lang-Imagn Images) Aiden Checketts · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 7:20 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Los Angeles Chargers finally got in the win column as they picked up their first win of the season, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on the road on Monday Night Football. After winning their first game of the 2026 season, it is going to be interesting to see how LA approaches the rest of the season , and whether they are competitive or end up with a top draft pick in the 2027 NFL Draft. That said, the focus now moves to their home matchup this week against the New York Jets in a game that could have a lot to do with how the draft order pans out. On that note, ESPN put out a Week 11 preview done by NFL Nation as well as fantasy football writer Eric Moody, analytics writer Seth Walder, and sports betting analyst Pamela Maldonado, who picked each game, and when it came to the Chargers and Jets matchup, LA was the unanimous pick. Now, in terms of the picks, Maldonado had the Chargers winning 24-20, Moody had a 23-17 victory for LA, and Walder picked Los Angeles to 23-20. All that to say, it is very clear that this ESPN panel does like the Chargers this week, and despite the fact the season has been rough for LA thus far, sometimes after picking up a win, a team can get into a rhythm and start stacking wins. One thing to note on the Chargers side, is the fact that they did a great job on the line of scrimmage on both sides of the ball on Monday night against the Ravens. Starting with the defense, LA held running back Derrick Henry to 10 yards rushing on 10 carries and the Ravens 15 attempts for 16 yards as a team. That is a great performance for LA and because of that, it forced quarterback Jacoby Brissett to put the the game on his shoulders and the Chargers were able to do just enough to get the win through picking him off once and recovering a fumble from wide receiver Zay Flowers. Now on the offensive side, the Chargers ran the ball very well with running back Omarion Hampton tallying 22 carries for 105 yards and one score in addition to quarterback Justin Herbert adding seven carries for 51 yards and a touchdown. As a team, LA ran the ball 34 times for 160 yards while averaging 4.7 yards per carry. All that to say, the formula for the Chargers in Week 10 was dominating on both sides of the line of scrimmage which worked out and enabled them to pick up a win which was huge for their confidence, but also shows that they do not need to lean on Herbert. So, as the Chargers prepare to take on the Jets in Week 11, it will be interesting to see if LA can pick up another win, but also what the formula might be, because if Los Angeles once again dominates up front, that could be something that the Chargers can lean on for the rest of the year.

picks.blurb: Latest Teams On Air Listen + Watch Contests Events More LISTEN LIVE Home The New York Jets will visit the Los Angeles Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET on Sunday in a game that has more implications for the draft than it does for… Ezra Bernstein Updated Nov 20, 2026 9:55 AM EST Share this story The New York Jets will visit the Los Angeles Chargers at 4:05 p.m. ET on Sunday in a game that has more implications for the draft than it does for the postseason. New York has lost five contests in a row, the last two of which were blowout defeats at the hands of the Kansas City Chiefs and the Buffalo Bills. While the Chargers are technically headed in the other direction after securing their first win of the year, Los Angeles still looks like one of the worst teams in football on a week-to-week basis. Getting a second consecutive win would be a good start in changing that perception. While New York is coming off a couple of blowout losses, those defeats did come against a few of the best teams in football. When head coach Aaron Glenn's squad faced teams like the New England Patriots, Miami Dolphins, and Las Vegas Raiders, the Jets hung tough, losing each game on the outcome of one or two plays. If those performances are any indication, New York should be plenty capable of keeping things close with the Chargers. Quarterback Geno Smith will have to play a turnover-free game, while the defense, led by rookie defensive end David Bailey, plays mistake-free football. Offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel finally seemed to get things to click in the Chargers' last game against the Baltimore Ravens. Giving running back Omarion Hampton an extended run for the first time in ages helped revive a ground attack that seemed dead in the water only a couple of weeks ago. If McDaniel knows what's good for his job security, he will give Hampton the touches he earned last week. Unfortunately, the offensive line did not fare as well in pass protection as it did in the run game, leaving quarterback Justin Herbert out to dry far too often. A fearsome New York defensive line will present an even bigger challenge than Baltimore did, making it difficult for the Chargers to win their second game of the year. away.headline: Geno Smith Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Jets QB's Status Ahead of Chargers Game
away.blurb: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will participate in Wednesday's practice in limited capacity after suffering multiple injuries in last Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . Smith left Sunday's game twice for a concussion evaluation and then for the ankle injury. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday Smith "underwent tests today that did not reveal anything major." "Smith, whose ankle provided the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week," Rapoport reported. The Jets are preparing to play Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers. Glenn confirmed earlier this week Smith will continue starting over Cade Klubnik if healthy. This article will be updated soon to provide more information and analysis.

away.blurb: Smith twice left the Jets’ 31-12 loss to Buffalo last Sunday, first to be evaluated for a head injury late in the first half and then after he hurt his left ankle during his only series of the third quarter. He was limited at practice earlier this week, but said Wednesday that he intended to play. In addition to Smith, Glenn said the team would evaluate how left guard Dylan Parham (knee), defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle), edge rusher Joseph Ossai (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) got through practice Friday before making final calls on their availability for the game. They were all listed as questionable and were full participants other than Phillips, who was limited. The offense will be down two wide receivers, though, with Glenn ruling out rookie Omar Cooper Jr. with ankle and hip injuries and Isaiah Williams with a rib injury. Neither was expected to practice Friday after sitting out the other practice sessions this week. Both were hurt against Buffalo. FLORHAM PARK, N.J. (AP) — New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith was a full participant at practice Friday and removed from the injury report, putting him on track to start against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. “He'll be practicing fully today, so we'll see how that goes,” coach Aaron Glenn said before practice Friday. “He looks solid. It's very encouraging.” The Jets (2-8) are looking to snap a five-game losing streak when they face the Chargers (1-8), who got their first win when they beat Baltimore on Monday night. Smith was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik last week. The fourth-round pick from Clemson would make his first NFL start if Smith can’t go, but that doesn't appear to be the case this week. “We've got two days to see how these guys operate,” Glenn said. “It is looking promising for all these guys, so I feel good about that.” The Jets have Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Tim Patrick and rookie Malik McClain as healthy wide receivers on the active roster. Sterling Shepard and Jamaal Pritchett are on the practice squad. Tight ends Mason Taylor and rookie Kenyon Sadiq could also see increased targets in the passing game. “I think that's the good thing about the tight end room is those guys can actually end up playing some of those receiver spots that we have,” Glenn said. Williams is the Jets' primary punt returner, so Isaiah Davis could assume that role. Williams also shares kickoff duties with Kene Nwangwu. Defensive lineman David Onyemata, on injured reserve the past eight weeks with an abdominal injury, won't be activated from injured reserve this week, Glenn said. The Jets opened Onyemata's 21-day practice window on Wednesday, so they have two more weeks before they need to either activate him or place him on season-ending IR. See AP’s full NFL coverage here

Even better is the week off should allow the Broncos to get players back from injury, especially on defense. All of this to say Denver is in a great spot. Now come the hated Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, led by rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza. The Broncos want to build on this great start to the season and carry the momentum over from the bye this Sunday against their rivals. Bo Nix and the Broncos offense can do their part by starting Sunday's game fast offensively and finishing drives with touchdowns. away.headline: Brock Bowers returns to practice ahead of Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 11 matchup against Denver Broncos
away.blurb: The Raiders’ leading receiver exited last week’s game against the Seattle Seahawks at halftime and missed Wednesday’s session with ankle and quadricep injuries. This was a step in the right direction for Bowers’ availability on Sunday against the Broncos, as the Raiders listed him as limited on the injury report (h/t The Athletic’s Sam Warren ). Also, Las Vegas’ offense really needs its top target. Additionally, Warren noted that guard Trey Zuhn III (illness), defensive tackle Tonka Hemingway (stinger) and defensive tackle Foley Fatukasi (toe) weren’t spotted during the media viewing period of Thursday’s practice. Zuhn wasn’t listed on Wednesday’s report, while Hemingway was a non-participant and Fatukasi was limited on Wednesday. Neither of the three linemen participated in Thursday’s session. Warren also reported that the Raiders brought in kickers Lucas Havrisik, Younghoe Koo and John Parker Romo for a workout, as Matt Gay is dealing with a hip injury and sat out of practice. Tight end Ian Thomas added an ankle injury to Thursday’s report after missing Wednesday with a calf injury, though Thomas was upgraded to limited on Thursday. As for the Broncos, they managed to get healthier for the second practice of the week. The only changes from yesterday’s injury report were cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine (ankle), defensive tackle Zach Allen (rest) and wide receiver Courtland Sutton (rest) going from limited to full participants. The Las Vegas Raiders received good news ahead of their Week 11 matchup against the Denver Broncos . ESPN’s Ryan McFadden posted a video of tight end Brock Bowers in full pads and participating in warmups ahead of Thursday’s practice, noting that Bowers is returning to the field. The ‘tight end’ has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns in eight games this season, leading the Silver and Black in all three categories despite missing the first two contests with a knee injury. According to Sumer Sports , the team’s passing game averages 0.105 EPA per pass and has a 49.0 percent success rate with Bowers on the field this year. Without him, those numbers dip to 0.005 EPA per pass and 43.4 percent. Factor in that rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza will be making his second career start against a Denver defense that ranks ninth in points per game allowed ( 20.7 ), and it’s even more important that Bowers suits up on Sunday. If Zuhn can’t go, second-year guard Caleb Rogers is likely the next man up. Rogers replaced Zuhn when the latter left the 49ers game with a concussion a couple of weeks ago. Hemingway’s and Fatukasi’s absence would really test the Raiders’ defensive tackle depth, a position that’s been an issue all season. That would likely mean more reps for Adam Butler, Tim Keenan III, Thomas Booker IV and JJ Pegues.

away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.headline: Will Brock Bowers play for the Raiders against the Broncos? What we know about the TE’s injury
away.blurb: The Raiders tight end returned to limited practice Thursday after missing Wednesday with ankle and quadriceps injuries. Bowers has been dealing with ankle and quadriceps injuries after leaving last Sunday’s 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His availability remains uncertain, but his return to the practice field is a positive development for the Raiders as they prepare for a difficult divisional matchup. As of Friday morning, November 20, Bowers has not been officially ruled in or out for Sunday’s game. However, his return to practice on Thursday has improved the outlook for his availability. The tight end was listed as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout. The Raiders listed both an ankle and a quadriceps injury on their report. Kubiak also indicated that Bowers might not need to practice this week to be available against Denver. His participation on Thursday nevertheless represents an important step toward a possible return. The Raiders are scheduled to practice again Friday , when another update on Bowers’ condition is expected. The team’s final injury report should provide a clearer indication of whether he will be available against the Broncos. He caught a pass after coming back onto the field, but the ankle continued to bother him and he was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Bowers finished with two receptions for 18 yards, a significant loss for the offense, who rely heavily on his ability to create opportunities in the passing game. His potential return would be significant for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is preparing for just his second NFL start . Bowers gives the young quarterback one of his most reliable targets against a Denver defense that has been among the league’s strongest this season. If Bowers is unavailable, Michael Mayer would be expected to take on a larger role in the Raiders’ offense. Mendoza has also highlighted the other options available to him, including wide receivers Jack Bech and Tre Tucker , as well as tight end Ian Thomas. The Raiders will hope Bowers can make enough progress to return against Denver, but his status will depend on how he responds to the remainder of the week’s practices. For now, Thursday’s limited participation is an encouraging sign . The Raiders are still waiting for confirmation that their star tight end will be ready to play on Sunday. home.headline: Will Brock Bowers play for the Raiders against the Broncos? What we know about the TE’s injury
home.blurb: The Raiders tight end returned to limited practice Thursday after missing Wednesday with ankle and quadriceps injuries. Bowers has been dealing with ankle and quadriceps injuries after leaving last Sunday’s 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. His availability remains uncertain, but his return to the practice field is a positive development for the Raiders as they prepare for a difficult divisional matchup. As of Friday morning, November 20, Bowers has not been officially ruled in or out for Sunday’s game. However, his return to practice on Thursday has improved the outlook for his availability. The tight end was listed as a limited participant in Thursday’s practice after missing Wednesday’s workout. The Raiders listed both an ankle and a quadriceps injury on their report. Kubiak also indicated that Bowers might not need to practice this week to be available against Denver. His participation on Thursday nevertheless represents an important step toward a possible return. The Raiders are scheduled to practice again Friday , when another update on Bowers’ condition is expected. The team’s final injury report should provide a clearer indication of whether he will be available against the Broncos. He caught a pass after coming back onto the field, but the ankle continued to bother him and he was eventually ruled out for the remainder of the contest. Bowers finished with two receptions for 18 yards, a significant loss for the offense, who rely heavily on his ability to create opportunities in the passing game. His potential return would be significant for rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza, who is preparing for just his second NFL start . Bowers gives the young quarterback one of his most reliable targets against a Denver defense that has been among the league’s strongest this season. If Bowers is unavailable, Michael Mayer would be expected to take on a larger role in the Raiders’ offense. Mendoza has also highlighted the other options available to him, including wide receivers Jack Bech and Tre Tucker , as well as tight end Ian Thomas. The Raiders will hope Bowers can make enough progress to return against Denver, but his status will depend on how he responds to the remainder of the week’s practices. For now, Thursday’s limited participation is an encouraging sign . The Raiders are still waiting for confirmation that their star tight end will be ready to play on Sunday. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. Q: Why has Trevor Lawrence been so surgical against zone coverage? Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. JS: There are several reasons. He has a group of pass-catchers in Jakobi Meyers, Parker Washington and Brenton Strange who all thrive at beating zone coverage thanks to their ability to find soft spots in zones and work the middle of the field. Liam Coen’s scheme also gives Lawrence and the passing game plenty of open looks against zone coverage, thanks to the balance they play with on offense and how they scheme open wide receivers. But most importantly, it comes down to how Lawrence is playing. He is confident in everything he is doing before and after the snap, far more confident than he has looked in past years. He knows where the ball is going, and he knows how to fit it in there regardless of how open or tight the passing windows are. Q: How does the potential absence of center Robert Hainsey affect the offensive line? Jacksonville Jaguars center Robert Hainsey | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JS: It will likely impact communication. The Jaguars’ offense has had some communication issues on the road this year, whether in Denver in Week 2 or in London in Weeks 5-6. JS: It will likely impact communication. The Jaguars’ offense has had some communication issues on the road this year, whether in Denver in Week 2 or in London in Weeks 5-6. That said, this might not be the crushing loss many outside Jacksonville believe it is. Hainsey has been the Jaguars’ fifth-best offensive lineman this season, and a lot of his value comes pre-snap. There is a real chance the Jaguars could see stronger play from second-year center Jonah Monheim, whom the staff rates extremely highly and who has played well in spot starts for Hainsey in the past. Q: What do you view as the key matchups, Giants offense vs. Jaguars defense and vice versa? Jacksonville Jaguars DB Travis Hunter | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: When it comes to the Jaguars’ defense vs. the Giants’ offense, the biggest matchup I am going to be watching is Malik Nabers against Travis Hunter. JS: When it comes to the Jaguars’ defense vs. the Giants’ offense, the biggest matchup I am going to be watching is Malik Nabers against Travis Hunter. Hunter has been a true shutdown No. 1 cornerback this season, even beyond his amazing athletic feats on his interceptions. He is the only Jaguars cornerback who can really run with Nabers, and I am fascinated to see these two battle downfield. The Jaguars don’t have their cornerbacks following receivers, but this might be the week to consider it. As for the Jaguars’ offense vs. the Giants’ defense, I am going with Walker Little against Abdul Carter. Little has played well for the Jaguars since stepping in as the starting left tackle a month ago due to injuries, but a player on Carter’s level hasn’t tested him. Little has proven he can get the job done week in and week out, but this week will be about proving that he can handle playing a blue-chip talent, which is exactly what he will need to do during a critical playoff run. Q: What’s the most underrated part/player of the Jaguars’ overall plan of attack? Jacksonville Jaguars defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect JS: Anthony Campanile. The Jaguars’ defensive coordinator is a genius, turning one of the NFL’s worst defenses into a powerhouse over the last two years. They are not flawless, since they still give up some explosive plays, and they do not get a ton of sacks. But Campanile has built one of the best run defenses in the NFL, and his philosophy of forcing quarterbacks to get the ball out of their hands quickly has led to plenty of takeaways and big plays. Campanile should be a future head coach, and the proof is in the pudding: he has helped elevate and evolve the Jaguars’ defense over the past two years. Q: The Jags have been blowing out opponents. What are your expectations for this week, though? Jacksonville Jaguars head coach Liam Coen | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect JS: I don’t think the Jaguars have a blowout this week, even though I believe they are firmly the better team. JS: I don’t think the Jaguars have a blowout this week, even though I believe they are firmly the better team. The Giants have fought hard week in and week out under John Harbaugh, and I think there is a real chance they take the fight to the Jaguars in the trenches. I think Trevor Lawrence will still be taking snaps in the fourth quarter this week, which has not been a given most weeks. There is a lot more respect in the Jaguars’ building right now than there was the last time these two teams played in 2022. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Jaguars, the full Week 11 slate Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 5:44 PM UTC · 7 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants face major test this week when they face the Jacksonville Jaguars. It is also a game that will provide a huge swing in the Giants' expected chances to make the playoffs. Will the Giants upset Jacksonville? See what our Big Blue View staff members think about that game and the rest of the Week 11 action in this week's staff picks. I don't think the Giants win this game. I think there's a path to a win for the Giants, if they can find it. The Giants are one of the very best teams in the NFL at forcing drives to end in punts. At the same time, the Jaguars will be without their starting center and the Giants are one of the best teams in the League at creating quick pressure. That's important because Trevor Lawrence has been one of the quarterbacks most affected by pressure in the NFL. At the same time, the Giants have rediscovered the explosive pass with J.J. McCarthy, which has been the weakness of the Jags' defense. If the Giants can score touchdowns while disrupting Lawrence, they've got the chance to come away with the upset. We've seen the Giants rebound after bad games, as well as play much better than anticipated when they're underdogs. Maybe both will happen here. The flip side of the coin is simpler and scarier to me: The Giants have one of the worst red zone defenses in the NFL, and the Jaguars have one of the best red zone offenses in the league. If the Giants can't stop them between the 20s, this game could get ugly fast. Pick: Jaguars Jacksonville is one of the hottest teams in the league with a young and explosive offense that can run the football. Their defense is aggressive but doesn't NEED to bring the blitz — they blitz at about a league-average rate, but Anthony Campanile does an excellent job utilizing simulated pressure to harass opposing quarterbacks. Jacksonville is third in offensive EPA, 4th in defensive EPA allowed, and 1st in Net EPA — they're a juggernaut based on their performance and the advanced analytics. Still, that doesn't mean the Giants don't have a chance — they just must play efficient football and avoid the catastrophic mistakes that have robbed them of wins. It's possible, but against the most efficient team in the NFL, it will be difficult. John Harbaugh will have the Giants ready and prepared for the game, and I believe it will be more exciting and competitive. Jacksonville is concluding their third straight road game, which could give the Giants a slight advantage at home, but I ultimately believe the better team finds a way to win. David Hartman It took 11 weeks, but for the first time this season, the Giants will face a team with a winning record when the 7-2 Jaguars come to town on Sunday. Not only is Jacksonville running away with the AFC South (they lead the division by four games), but they're steamrolling the competition. They've won their last three games by a combined 75 points. This is easily Big Blue's toughest test of the season, so far. Jacksonville is very good on both sides of the ball. They're fourth in offensive DVOA, third in defensive DVOA, and third in overall DVOA. They also have an excellent field goal kicker with crazy range. If you look at both rosters, it's hard to find clear advantages for the Giants at any position group outside of tight end, and even there, Jacksonville has good players. Can the Giants win this game? Yes. They're at home, they're getting an extra three days of rest, and as we saw when they played Houston, they aren't scared and can surprise as a big underdog. They'll need to dial it up on defense and pressure Trevor Lawrence into the kinds of mistakes he used to make before Liam Coen got there. They also might have a little extra motivation after letting last week's game against the Commanders slip away at the end. I won't be surprised if John Harbaugh's team hangs in there and keeps it as a one-score game most of the way. But in the end, until the Giants show me that they can beat a really good team, I can't pick them to do so. Tony Del Genio You can talk yourself into believing that the Giants can beat Jacksonville this Sunday. They needed a miraculous last-second 57-yard field goal to beat the Eagles team (with Jalen Hurts) that the Giants defeated (without Hurts). They lost to the Texans team that the Giants beat the following week. The woeful Titans were within a TD against them last week with 5 minutes left. So indeed, it could be a competitive game. Unfortunately, the Jags have also won games by 24, 29, 35, and 23 points this season. They have scored 31 or more in each of their past four games, and over 40 in two of those. The Giants have only scored more than 30 points once, and only then because of a 99-yard pick-6 on the last play of the game. Trevor Lawrence isn't necessarily playing any better this year than in the past. He's a QB that simultaneously makes great passes and puts the ball up for grabs, yet unlike in years past, he's cut down on the INTs while getting the TDs. Part of that may be due to 5'10" wide receiver Parker Washington (a 2023 6th-round pick), who had a breakout 2025 and is on pace for 1,000 yards. Running back Bhayshul Tuten, a 4th round 2025 pick, isn't quite in the Jahmyr Gibbs – Kenneth Walker class but he's not far below and is a missed tackle machine. A lot of the credit has to go to head coach Liam Coen, who also calls the plays and turned this team around as soon as he was hired. Lawrence, like most QBs, has trouble with pressure, but he is not too fazed by the blitz. Finding a way to disrupt his rhythm is a key to any chance the Giants may have. On defense, the Jaguars are strong at linebacker with fourth-round 2023 pick Ventrell Miller, one of the league's best (note how many mid-round picks the Jags have hit on), along with Foyesade Oluokun. They also put on a decent pass rush with Josh Hines-Allen, Travon Walker, and Dennis Gardeck. In the secondary, Travis Hunter is playing more like a No. 2 pick, having mostly given up his evening gig as a receiver. Are the Giants a serious playoff contender? This is the type of game they can use to make a statement against a team that is in the Super Bowl conversation. I think they'll put up a fight. I also don't think they're there yet. Pick : Jaguars Valentine's View I want to convince myself to pick the Giants to defeat the Jaguars. I really do. I just can't. The Jaguars are a team with justifiable Super Bowl ambitions . They are a well-rounded team with a high-powered offense, a very good defense, and one of the best field-goal kickers in the business in Cam Little. The Giants are a good team. They are resilient. They will give the Jaguars their best shot. Maybe, just maybe, it will be good enough to pull off an upset that would go a long way toward ensuring that the Giants make the playoffs. I just can't pick them to do it.
