picks.blurb: NFL Week 11 picks and predictions, straight-up and ATS: Jaguars blow past Giants, Vikings stay hot with Kirk - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Jacksonville Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence | GettyImages | Illustration by Michael Castillo Cody Williams · FanSided Wed, November 18, 2026 at 12:50 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads I'm not going to lie to you, NFL Week 11 isn't exactly loaded with marquee matchups. Teams like the Chicago Bears , Buffalo Bills , Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos - you know, the contenders in this league right now - are all matched up with teams well out of the playoff race. Throw in the fact that six teams are on bye, and the schedule gets leaner. But we do have two big-time matchups with the Jacksonville Jaguars visiting the New York Giants and then a huge Sunday Night Football showdown in Mexico City with the Minnesota Vikings taking on the San Francisco 49ers for NFC supremacy. But regardless of the quality of matchup, we have every game covered in our NFL picks and predictions. We're coming off of two winning weeks in a row and are getting our mojo back. Surely a week in which there are numerous double-digit spreads with heavy and deserved favorites won't come back to haunt us. But here we go, once again delivering with NFL picks for Week 11 with predictions for every game straight-up and against the spread. NFL Week 11 predictions: Picks straight-up and ATS for every game Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington, quarterback Trevor Lawrence | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect NFL Week 11 Matchup Straight-Up Pick Colts vs. Texans (TNF) Saints vs. Bears Ravens vs. Panthers Panthers -2.5 Dolphins vs. Bills Titans vs. Cowboys Cardinals vs. Chiefs Buccaneers vs. Lions Buccaneers +6.5 Steelers vs. Eagles Steelers -4.5 Jets vs. Chargers Raiders vs. Broncos Jaguars vs. Giants Vikings vs. 49ers (SNF) Bengals vs. Commanders 2026 NFL Picks Straight-Up Record: 95-57 (Last week 11-3) | ATS Record: 71-78-3 (Last week 9-5) Note: All lines are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook. Game odds refresh periodically and are subject to change. If you or someone you know has a gambling problem and wants help, call 1-800-GAMBLER. Toughest NFL Week 11 prediction to make Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kirk Cousins | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Minnesota Vikings (+3) vs. San Francisco 49ers - in Mexico City Point blank, these are two of the three best teams in the NFC right now. So you throw in the fact that this game is at a neutral site in primetime and it makes it even more difficult. Looking at these two teams, though, people are going to look at the 49ers and their high-powered offense and be intrigued by that. But the Vikings have proven that, under Brian Flores, they're capable of slowing down anyone. Heck, the Lions and Packers both found that out - even if the Detroit got the win thanks to Kyler Murray. But now Kirk Cousins is back in the fold for Minnesota and we've seen him already step in and raise the baseline of the Vikings offense substantially. Who knew getting Justin Jefferson the ball was the smart play? It's that end of the field that ended up being my deciding factor here, though. The fact that the Vikings offense has found this new level of competency complements the defense so incredibly well. Moreover, the 49ers defense, though talented, hasn't exactly been infallible of late. So in Mexico City, give me the Vikings staying hot and establishing a foothold in the NFC. Easiest NFL Week 11 pick on the board Chicago Bears wide receiver Luther Burden III, quarterback Caleb Williams | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect New Orleans Saints at Chicago Bears (-11.5) This feels scarily too easy. Like, have oddsmakers watched the Saints recently? This defense is struggling mightily right now and the offense isn't exactly lighting the world on fire anymore either. To add to that, the Bears have been clinical more often than not this season (the last time out against the Buccaneers where Caleb Williams couldn't stop throwing picks, notwithstanding). Now we get Ben Johnson and this team coming out of a bye where they've had time to gameplan and get healthier. Yeah, that's all lining up pretty heavily toward Chicago for me, especially with this game being played in the Windy City. It's not that I think this game will end up being just a mauling on the Bears' part (though that's also not out of the question). The Saints should be able to score a bit. But it feels like Chicago will just have more consistent and perhaps unstopped success that will ultimately allow them to pull away handily. The pick that probably has you scratching your head Tampa Bay Buccaneers running back Bucky Irving | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tampa Bay Buccaneers (+6.5) at Detroit Lions Yes, I'm aware that Baker Mayfield's health is (once again) in question coming into this game. That's not me saying I have full faith in Jalon Daniels getting back into the offense, though he didn't play that poorly when he had to step in earlier in the season. What I think people are overlooking in this matchup is the fact that the Lions are coming off of the win in Munich and now have to travel back across the country and not get a bye week between games. That has happened for eight teams this season, traveling back from Europe and playing again in one week, and those teams are 2-5-1 straight-up, much less against the spread favored by more than a touchdowns. When you then factor in losing Aidan Hutchinson last week and what that could mean for Detroit's defense - which I wasn't exactly over the moon about to begin with - there's a path here for the Bucs to keep this close. I'll still take the Lions to win straight-up, mainly because I'm a coward and understand they are the substantially better team in this matchup. However, I do think the Buccaneers keep the game within a possession when we get to the end of it. Jacksonville Jaguars running back Travis Etienne Jr. (1) celebrates his first quarter touchdown with quarterback Trevor Lawrence (16) during a game against the New York Giants at EverBank Field in on Oct. 23, 2022. What happened last week? The Jaguars beat the Tennessee Titans 40-23 in Nashville. The Giants lost to Washington 24-21. What are the Jaguars-Giants odds? The Jaguars are 6-point favorites, according to BetMGM . They're -275 on the money line. The Giants are +225. The over-under is 46.5 points. Who's injured? Jaguars: Out — C Robert Hainsey (knee), DE B.J. Green (forearm). Questionable — DT Matt Dickerson (neck), DE Danny Striggow (concussion). Giants: The Giants are not reporting any players out or questionable. What's the series history between the Jaguars and Giants? The two teams are tied 4-4. New York is 3-1 vs. the Jaguars at home. The last time the Jaguars played the Giants at MetLife Stadium was in 2018, when they won 20-15 . The last time the Jaguars played at MetLife Stadium was on Dec. 22, 2022, when they beat the New York Jets 19-3 . What happened the last time the Jaguars played the Giants? Christian Kirk was tackled just short of the goal line and the Giants won 23-17 on Oct. 23, 2022, in Jacksonville. Trevor Lawrence threw for 310 yards and Kirk caught seven passes for 96 yards. What's the key Jaguars-Giants matchup? Jaguars DT Jordan Davis vs. Giants RB Cam Skattebo With a chance of rain on Sunday in East Rutherford, the game might turn into a low-scoring battle, with running the ball and the ability to stop the run the key to winning. Expect a few collisions between Skattebo, the Giants' leading rusher (496 yards, 4.3 per carry) and Davis, the Jaguars' acquisition from Philadelphia two weeks ago who will be playing his first game for the Jags. J.J. McCarthy (18) of the New York Giants is sacked by Jordan Davis of the Philadelphia Eagles during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field on Nov. 8, 2026 in Philadelphia. Davis will be playing his second game in a row against the Giants. His last game as an Eagle was a 19-11 loss to New York on Nov. 8, but he played well, with two tackles for losses and a sack. Skattebo was injured and did not play in that game, but last week he had 78 yards rushing and two touchdowns and three receptions for 44 yards in the loss to Washington. What's notable about Jaguars vs. Giants? The Jaguars are playing their third straight road game, which has happened six times in franchise history. The Jaguars are 5-1 in those games, with four of the five victories coming in playoff seasons. ... The Jaguars won the first two games, at Baltimore and Tennessee. They've swept three-game road trips twice, in 2001 and 2005. ... This will be the sixth time in eight weeks that the Jaguars have played away from Jacksonville, counting the two London games. ... If the Jaguars win, they will be 10-3 on the road under coach Liam Coen . The only NFL coaches to win 10 or more road games in fewer games over the past 25 years are Mike Macdonald and Sean McVay with 11 each. ... Lawrence has set a franchise record with seven consecutive games of a 95.0 or better passer rating. It's also the longest current active streak in the NFL. ... The Jaguars are 5-9 overall in East Rutherford against both the Giants and the Jets. away.blurb: The Athletic's Dan Duggan added: "Seems like Jacksonville's RB is headed toward a questionable status" Shipley wrote: "No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. home.headline: Giants Cam Skattebo Reveals Backflip Celebration's Future After Aidan Hutchinson's Knee Injury
home.blurb: Cam Skattebo is retiring the backflip. The New York Giants' running back said he will no longer do his signature celebration after seeing Detroit Lions' pass-rusher Aidan Hutchinson tear his ACL during a sack celebration on Sunday. "It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters Monday. "I'm saying yeah [no more backflips]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me." He did add that he might bring back the backflip "if we go to the playoffs or something," but acknowledged that Hutchinson "didn't think about [the risk] either, and it happened." You have to think folks with the Giants' organization were jumping for joy—backflipping for joy, even—after hearing Skattebo's comments on the matter.

LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel. We simulated the rest of the season using PFN’s NFL Playoff Predictor. 🔮 Here’s the projected playoff bracket 👀 pic.twitter.com/QBo8zogNJ6 There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year. Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium. The Vikings are set to face the San Francisco 49ers in a neutral site game in Mexico City, and there are a ton of playoff implications at stake. Not only are the Vikings battling for first place in the NFC North, but a win over San Fran would give Minnesota a legit shot at the No. 1 seed in the conference. A Cousins trade materialized for Minnesota after back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo where Kyler Murray (against Detroit) and Carson Wentz (against Buffalo) showed that they simply aren’t playing quarterback at a high enough level for the Vikings to win a Super Bowl. That sentiment has changed in the futures market, as the Vikings are now priced around 15/1 to win it all after an upset win over Green Bay in Week 10. The odds for that game shifted in a big way after Cousins was acquired, as the same goes for Week 11 against San Francisco. Sports Illustrated spoke to several oddsmakers this week to see just how much the Cousins’ acquisition has changed the Vikings’ outlook in this Sunday Night matchup. How Much Kirk Cousins Impacts Vikings vs. 49ers Odds for NFL Week 11 The Vikings opened as 3.5-point underdogs in Week 11 after their win over Green Bay, but that line has continued to move towards the Vikings, settling at 3. While that’s a minor move, there’s a chance this line would have been set as far as 49ers -7 if Murray or Wentz was under center on Sunday night. “Well, if the quarterback play continued to go the way it was before Cousins arrived, the Vikings would have been close to a touchdown underdog, rather than a field goal underdog,” Johnny Avello, Director of Race and Sports Operations for DraftKings Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. That’s at least a four-point swing in favor of the 49ers, though not every book had that price. BetMGM and FanDuel both told Sports Illustrated that the spread would likely be close to four or five. “Not too much believe it or not, probably was about a point or so move,” Christian Cipollini, Senior Trading Manager at BetMGM , told Sports Illustrated. The reason being is there isn't a major gap between Cousins and Murray. The main reason for this spread being close is the strength of the defense. Both QBs are capable, it helps Minnesota's future odds more because if one gets injured they have a capable backup to come in.” It’s interesting to hear about different pricing across the industry, as Fanatics has a much different grade – but similar to DraftKings – when it comes to the Murray vs. Cousins debate: “We opened up a lookahead line on the day of trade deadline day, it was plus seven,” Ty Gour, Sports Trader at Fanatics Sportsbook , told Sports Illustrated. “And now the Vikings are three-point dogs, just to give you an idea of how highly we rate Kirk Cousins versus Murray or Wentz.” In his first start with the Vikings, Cousins threw for 207 yards, two scores and one pick, and he has 22 touchdown passes in the 2026 season. There’s no doubt that this Vikings team – which has the No. 2 defense in EPA/Play in 2026 – has a much better chance of competing with San Fran’s No. 1 offense with Cousins calling the shots. What Would the Vikings vs. 49ers Spread Be in San Francisco? This game is also unusual because of the neutral site aspect. While this is technically a home game for San Francisco, it likely would be favored by more Levi’s Stadium in Santa Clara. Still, Avello explained that home field doesn’t matter as much as it used to when DraftKings sets the spread for games. “ The Niners playing at home – there's a misconception with home-field advantage,” Avello said. When you look at it across the league, it's only a couple of points. Some teams get a little stronger, and a lot of it has to do with weather. So, the Niners would have been only maybe another point and a half at home, so maybe the line would have been 4.5.” San Francisco is a perfect 5-0 at home in the 2026 season, so it’ll be interesting to see if Kyle Shanahan’s team can hold up on a neutral field. The 49ers (8-1) are looking to maintain their lead in the NFC and NFC West, but a loss to Minnesota would bring it back down into the same playing field with other two-loss teams like Chicago and Detroit. picks.blurb: Justin Jefferson Given Bold Superlative in Vikings vs. 49ers Preview - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Justin Jefferson Given Bold Superlative in Vikings vs. 49ers Preview (Brad Rempel-Imagn Images) Joey Hickey · Roundtable Sports Fri, November 20, 2026 at 12:00 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Minnesota Vikings (7-2) made a statement last Sunday. The Vikings went out and defeated the Green Bay Packers (6-4) in Lambeau Field, 30-10. If you stopped paying attention two weeks ago, you're probably wondering how that happened. In short, the Vikings traded for quarterback Kirk Cousins and kept its defensive dominance intact. The result? A complete dismantling of a rival that has had the upper hand for the better part of the rivalry. Ahead for the Vikings is the team's biggest test of the season. Minnesota will take on the best team in the NFC. They will have to do so in Mexico City. Steve Silverman of Athlon Sports discussed how the Vikings could make an even bigger statement in their game against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City. To do so, they could use a big game from star wide receiver Justin Jefferson. Here's some of what Silverman had to say on Jefferson's effect on the matchup. "There was no player who needed to see improvement at the QB position more than Jefferson. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz failed to get the ball to Jefferson in the first half of the season, but that immediately changed with Cousins under center. Jefferson was targeted 13 times in that game and he caught 9 passes for 74 yards. He needs to do even more in this game. Jefferson needs at least one big play in this game to help his team play effectively on offense. Jefferson caught a 97-yard TD pass the last time the Vikings played the Niners in Week 2 of the 2024 season. That play stunned San Francisco and the Vikings were able to dictate the pace. A big play early in the game from Jefferson could give Minnesota the edge in this game." Cousins' emergence opened up a world of possibilities for the Vikings offense, but one of the big changes could involve Jefferson regaining the production he had in Cousins' first stint with Minnesota. We saw flashes of what things could look like against the Packers. Nobody is going to confuse the Vikings for one of the best operating offenses in the NFL, but a couple of explosive plays to Jefferson could mean the difference between a narrow Vikings loss and Minnesota building a two-score lead that its defense won't squander. We'll keep an eye on how the Vikings utilize Jefferson in the consequential matchup on Sunday.

The Vikings are scheduled to visit the Patriots at Gillette Stadium on December 10 for Thursday Night Football. That game comes just four days after Minnesota's Week 13 meeting with the Carolina Panthers. A matchup originally featuring Maye against Brian Flores' defense now appears far more likely to feature New England's backup quarterback. away.headline: 49ers vs. Vikings marks NFL's return to Mexico City, though the league never truly left
away.blurb: Many fans will no doubt view Sunday's matchup between the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings as marking the NFL's return to Mexico. "I fell in love with the 49ers in the mid-80s because of Joe Montana. I've attended every game held in Mexico, and it's great that they're back," said Octavio Zúñiga, a 50-year-old fan. "Last time (in 2022), they came out carrying the Mexican flag as they entered the stadium. That commitment to the Mexican fan base is truly appreciated." November 19, 2026 / 2:43 PM PST / AP The reality is, the league never truly left. Although Mexico last hosted a regular-season game in 2022, the league's growth in the country has been steady, according to Arturo Olivé, managing director of NFL Mexico. Over the past 18 years, the league's domestic fan base has surged from roughly 10 million to 40 million, according to the NFL. "We have grown significantly over these years thanks to the constant, continuous, daily work of our team," Olivé said. "Eighteen years ago, we chose our battles and focused our attention on the specific areas we needed to improve in order to expand our fan base." In Mexico, the NFL trails only soccer — the national sport — in total fans. The game's popularity is no coincidence; American football is as much a part of Mexican sports tradition as soccer, boxing, and lucha libre. The Mexico game will be the last of the nine international NFL games played this season, a league record. To expand its reach, NFL Mexico invested heavily in flag football, which has steadily gained traction and now boasts roughly 4 million players nationwide. While impressive, Olivé acknowledges that in a nation of more than 130 million people, there is still vast room for growth. To accelerate adoption, the league signed an agreement with the National Commission of Physical Culture and Sport (CONADE) to expand the sport across public schools. "With 4 million children in the program, we are barely scratching the surface. Forty million fans in Mexico is a lot, but there are still another 80 or 90 million people we could reach," Olivé said. CONADE, the agency that oversees Mexico's federal sports budget, is eager to promote flag football ahead of its debut as an Olympic sport at the 2028 Los Angeles Games. Mexico's women's national team has already secured an Olympic berth. "We believe this alliance turns schools into spaces for participation, well-being and talent development," said Rommel Pacheco, general director of CONADE. "We want more girls, boys, and young people to play an accessible and inclusive sport." Olivé noted that initiatives such as flag football and Play 60 have been particularly effective at drawing women to the game. Today, women account for 47% of Mexico's 40 million NFL fans. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray are out as expected, while just Jay Ward and Isaiah Rodgers are listed as questionable. Kevin O’Connell said that Rodgers felt good in Friday’s practice but was limited, and they will see how he feels after practice and with post-practice treatment. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. picks.blurb: Bengals vs. Commanders odds, expert picks, and our prediction for Week 11 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football James Harden drops 51 in Cavs’ NBA Cup win over Pacers TRENDING Maye reportedly fractures fibula Report: Dodgers get Royce Lewis Kane to miss multiple months Puka Nacua suspended 'GTA 6' impacts sports Patrick Judis · SB Nation Fri, November 20, 2026 at 11:30 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Cincinnati Bengals have been one of the hottest teams in the NFL and are tied with a handful of teams with a five-game win streak. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! It was in Week 3 of the 2024 season—Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels' rookie season. The Commanders, led by a nearly perfect game from Daniels, shocked the Bengals on the road, 38-33. Daniels' late fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin was one of the top plays of that season. On Monday, the Bengals meet the Commanders again in prime time. Cincinnati enters Monday night's game 7-2 and winners of five in a row. Quarterback Joe Burrow is playing at an MVP level, completing almost 75% of his passes, with 2,795 passing yards, 27 touchdowns and six interceptions. He's coming off a win over Pittsburgh, where he passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns. So, it's no surprise that the Bengals opened as solid 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders. Washington's record (3-5-1) may not show it, but the Commanders have been playing better football recently. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is quietly having an excellent bounce-back season, playing with a dislocated left elbow and dealing with numerous injuries around him. The Commanders' defense got off to a rough start under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, but has looked like a different unit over the last few weeks. On Monday, they'll have their biggest test of the year, defending Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. While oddsmakers have the Bengals as favorites, so do NFL analysts. NFL.com analysts predicted the outcome of Monday's Week 11 game between the Commanders and Bengals. All 10 picks were in favor of Cincinnati. That's not really a surprise. However, one analyst predicted that the Bengals will defeat the Commanders 63-21. Cincinnati is certainly capable of putting up a lot of points against Washington. 63? Don't count on it. Head coach Dan Quinn should post that graphic in the Commanders' locker room for everyone to see this week.
